sources: Sun Aug 23 weekend run, capturing Friday Aug 21 closes. Reconciled against the repo's own GitHub Actions auto-update of Aug 21 (FRED/Yahoo) - market series taken from that feed where it is authoritative, macro releases refreshed by hand where the feed was carrying stale prints. THEME: the reflation trade came roaring back while the US hard data quietly stabilised - crude, gold and freight all repriced higher in the same week that claims, permits and the LEI all improved. THE STORY IS THE COMMODITY COMPLEX: Brent 94.35 Aug 21, UP 6.6% from 88.52 a week ago and through the first 90 threshold for the first time this cycle - the Strait of Hormuz risk premium built through the whole week rather than fading, with Brent holding near 94 and WTI steady. Gold 4,607/oz Aug 21 (TradingEconomics), UP 2.03% on the day alone and ~5% on the week from 4,388 - a genuine flight-to-quality bid, not a dollar story. Copper 6.58/lb essentially unchanged from 6.59, so copper/gold falls to 1.41 from 1.50, the sharpest one-week deterioration in the growth mix since the spring: gold is doing all the work, copper none. DXY 98.81 Aug 21, DOWN from 99.80 and a three-month low - dollar weakness is amplifying the commodity move rather than causing it. BDTI ~3004 Aug 21 (derived from StockQ YTD +127.75% and Barchart BDTI.BI base 1319; +/-20pts, MA5 2929 corroborates), UP ~260pts or ~9.5% on the week and the highest print of the cycle - freight remains the deepest red reading on the board and is now confirming the crude move. NOTE: the automated feed was carrying 2742 for BDTI; refreshed here. AGAINST THAT, THE US DATA IMPROVED ACROSS THE BOARD: initial jobless claims 206k for the week ending Aug 15 (DOL, released Aug 20), DOWN 6k and a beat vs 210k consensus, though the prior week was revised up 209k->212k and continuing claims rose 18k to 1,799k - the sub-200k streak has not returned but the labour market is not cracking either. Building permits 1,443k July SAAR (Census/HUD, released Aug 18), UP 5.0% m/m from a revised 1,374k and +3.1% y/y - the strongest housing datapoint in months. Conference Board LEI +0.2% m/m in July to 99.5 (released Aug 20) after a revised -0.1% in June; the six-month growth rate turned POSITIVE (+0.2% Jan-Jul) for the first time in over four years, implying y/y approximately -1.1% vs -1.4% previously - consumer expectations remain the single largest drag. All three were stale in the automated feed and are refreshed here. THE VOL COMPLEX WOKE UP, MILDLY: VIX 15.31 Aug 21, UP from 14.25 and off the 2026 low, having printed 16.01 intraweek. MOVE 73.2 Aug 20/21 (MacroMicro/Yahoo ^MOVE), UP from 69.6 - both gauges rising off cycle lows but still deeply benign in absolute terms. 10Y-2Y +0.51 Aug 21 (10Y 4.74 vs 2Y 4.24), unchanged w/w - the bear-steepening paused, 10Y +3bp on the day on the crude move. T5YIFR 2.30% (FRED; 5Y breakeven 2.21, 10Y 2.24), flat w/w - breakevens are NOT validating the oil spike, which continues to argue this is a supply-side/geopolitical premium rather than a demand impulse. HY OAS 271bp, flat and still pinned in the richest decile ~180bp inside the long-run median - credit has now ignored both the UMich collapse and the oil spike. WATCH THIS FOR THE FIRST CRACK. CARRIED VALUES: NFCI -0.55 (Chicago Fed week ending Aug 14 was published Aug 19 but the value could not be retrieved from a free source this run; carried from Aug 7 - with HY at 271 and vol near lows, conditions are unlikely to have tightened). EUR/USD 3M xccy -10bp carried, no free dated quote, secondary estimates cluster -16 to -20bp with no stress event in the window. SOFR-OIS ~2bp carried, SOFR itself 3.63% Aug 20 (NY Fed), no funding stress. UMich consumer sentiment 51.0 carried - that is the August PRELIMINARY print from Aug 14; the final lands Aug 28 and is the key thing to watch. ISM Manufacturing 55.6 July carried, August prints Sep 1. Sahm Rule -0.03 July carried, no labour-recession trigger, August prints Sep 4. Global liquidity 1=stable: the Fed ended QT in December 2025 while the ECB continues balance-sheet reduction through 2026 - divergent, net neutral. WATCH THIS WEEK: NFCI Aug 26, jobless claims Aug 27, UMich final Aug 28, ISM Sep 1.
